symbols.name: V0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal V_0=\{0\}\cup\mathcal V\), where \(0\) denotes no exposure or no infection

symbols.name: delta
symbols.role: upper bound on the fraction of noninfected period-one exposees whose later controlled response is altered by that exposure

symbols.name: DeltaRange
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D\subseteq[0,1]\) is a nonempty closed range fixed from scientific validation evidence; absent a randomized or controlled validation substudy, the default report uses \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\)
symbols.role: scientifically justified range over which identified sets and sign conclusions are reported

symbols.name: omegaPrime
symbols.role: perturbed policy/reference mixture used to reevaluate the challenge-risk ratio on the fixed observed-data fiber

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: \(R=(R_1,R_2^{[\cdot]})\), where \(R_{1av}\) is infection under assignment \(a\) and a period-one controlled challenge by variant \(v\); \(R^{[0]}_{2av}\) is the period-two controlled response after no period-one exposure, and \(R^{[u]}_{2av}\), \(u\in\mathcal V\), is the period-two controlled response after a period-one exposure to \(u\) that did not infect
symbols.role: controlled challenge response type allowing noninfecting-exposure priming

symbols.name: S
symbols.space: \((\mathcal V_0^{\mathcal T})^{\mathcal A}\times\{0,1\}^{\mathcal A\times\mathcal V}\times\{0,1\}^{\mathcal V_0\times\mathcal A\times\mathcal V}\)
symbols.role: joint exposure-history and history-indexed challenge-response type

symbols.name: Ja
symbols.def: \(J^a_t\) is the first-infection strain in period \(t\) under assignment \(a\) and natural exposure history \(H^a\)

symbols.name: g
symbols.role: first-infection-by-variant observation map allowing a noninfecting period-one exposure to alter the period-two response

symbols.name: J
symbols.def: \(J_t=v\) records first infection by variant \(v\) in period \(t\), while \(J_t=0\) records no first infection

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: \(q_{tv}=\Pr(H_t^0=v)\) in an external exposure sample from the trial environment

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: \(\rho_{1a}(x,\omega)=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}\omega_v r_{1av}(s)x_s\) and \(\rho_{2a}(x,\omega)=\sum_{s\in\mathcal S}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}\omega_v r^{[0]}_{2av}(s)x_s\)
symbols.role: reference-mixture controlled challenge risk, with the period-two target defined after no period-one exposure

symbols.name: CSEpub
symbols.def: For \(K=2\), \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm P}_t(x)=\{\rho_{t1}(x,e^{(1)})/\rho_{t0}(x,e^{(1)})\}/\{\rho_{t1}(x,e^{(2)})/\rho_{t0}(x,e^{(2)})\}\) whenever its component denominators are positive.
symbols.role: Perényi--Stensrud marginal challenge subtype effect expressed through point-mass controlled challenge risks

symbols.name: hobs
symbols.def: \(h_{tav}^{\mathrm{obs}}(b)=b_{tav}/\{1-\sum_{r<t}\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}b_{raw}\}\) whenever the at-risk denominator is positive.

symbols.name: CSEobs
symbols.def: For \(K=2\), \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm{obs}}_t(b)=\{h_{t,1,1}^{\mathrm{obs}}(b)/h_{t,0,1}^{\mathrm{obs}}(b)\}/\{h_{t,1,2}^{\mathrm{obs}}(b)/h_{t,0,2}^{\mathrm{obs}}(b)\}\) whenever its component denominators are positive.
symbols.role: observed hazard-ratio functional identifying the marginal challenge subtype effect under the Perényi--Stensrud conditions

symbols.name: Psi
symbols.role: extended reference-mixture vaccine challenge-risk ratio correspondence

symbols.name: Mfull
symbols.role: compatible full laws at the disclosed priming-sensitivity value

symbols.name: Ppoly
symbols.role: reduced compatible-history fiber at the disclosed priming-sensitivity value

symbols.name: CC
symbols.role: homogenized endpoint program at the disclosed priming-sensitivity value

symbols.name: ThetaI
symbols.type: subset of the extended nonnegative line
symbols.role: sharp identified set for the vaccine challenge-risk ratio at sensitivity value \(\delta\)

symbols.name: ThetaIRange
symbols.type: subset of the extended nonnegative line

symbols.name: qcase
symbols.role: case-substituted exposure margin that preserves the external exposure rate but replaces its variant composition

symbols.name: VE
symbols.role: biological vaccine effect under the common reference mixture

symbols.name: Eomega
symbols.def: \(E_\omega\) has columns indexed by \(s\in\overline{\mathcal S}\) and equality rows \(1\), \(\widetilde g_{tav}(s)\), \(\mathbf 1\{h_t^0=v\}\), and \(p_\omega(s)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}\omega_v\{r_{10v}(s)-r^{[0]}_{20v}(s)\}\)

symbols.name: Fdelta
symbols.def: \(F_\delta\) has columns indexed by \(s\in\overline{\mathcal S}\) and rows indexed by \((a,u,v)\in\mathcal A\times\mathcal V\times\mathcal V\), with entry \(f_{\delta,auv}(s)=\mathbf 1\{h_1^0=u,r_{1au}=0\}\bigl[\mathbf 1\{r^{[u]}_{2av}\neq r^{[0]}_{2av}\}-\delta\bigr]\)

symbols.name: dvec
symbols.def: \(d(b,q)=(1,(b_{tav})_{t,a,v},(q_{tv})_{t,v},0)^{\top}\), ordered as the equality rows of \(E_\omega\)
symbols.role: right-hand side of the common-history constraints

symbols.name: eta
symbols.role: free dual multiplier for common-history equality constraints

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.role: dual multiplier for priming-sensitivity inequalities in minimization programs

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.role: free dual multiplier for common-history equality constraints in sign separation

symbols.name: mu
symbols.role: dual multiplier for priming-sensitivity inequalities in sign separation

symbols.name: SK2
symbols.type: finite set of four latent types
symbols.role: worked two-variant compatible support with no priming and hence validity for every \(\delta\in[0,1]\)

symbols.name: xK2
symbols.def: \(x_\star^{(2)}(s_{ij})=1/4\) for every \(s_{ij}\in\mathcal S_\star^{(2)}\), with zero mass elsewhere

symbols.name: rStar
symbols.def: When \(U_\delta(b,q,\omega)<1\), let \(r_\star(\delta)=\min\{\lVert\omega'-\omega\rVert_1:\omega'\in\Delta(\mathcal V),\ x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega),\ \rho_{11}(x,\omega')\geq\rho_{21}(x,\omega')\}\). When \(L_\delta(b,q,\omega)>1\), reverse the displayed inequality. The minimum of the empty set is \(+\infty\); if neither strict baseline frontier holds, set \(r_\star(\delta)=0\).
symbols.role: common-law mixture radius at which the strict baseline ratio sign first ceases to be uniform, pointwise in the priming sensitivity value

symbols.name: Cn
symbols.type: random closed subset of the extended nonnegative line
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{n,m,\delta}^{\mathrm{exact}}\) is the exact multinomial projection in \(\text{def:exact-whole-set-projection}\)
symbols.role: exact whole-set confidence projection at the disclosed priming-sensitivity value

standard.name: No effect of vaccination on exposure

assumptions.condition: For every \(t\in\mathcal T\), \(a\in\mathcal A\), and \(v\in\mathcal V\), \(\mathbf 1\{J_t^a=v\}=\widetilde g_{tav}(S)\) almost surely.

novel.justification: The response map records first infection while permitting the period-two controlled response to depend on the identity of a prior noninfecting exposure. It retains arbitrary dependence among exposure histories and controlled susceptibilities and does not impose no priming.

The parameter \(\delta\) bounds the fraction of noninfected exposees whose later controlled response is altered by that exposure. The value \(\delta=0\) recovers no priming and \(\delta=1\) permits unrestricted priming. Routine negative tests or serial serology do not identify a small value; absent a randomized or controlled validation substudy, \(\delta\) is reported as a sensitivity parameter over \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(t\in\mathcal T\) and \(v\in\mathcal V_0\), the external exposure sample has margin \(q_{tv}=\Pr(H_t^0=v)\) in the trial target population.

standard.name: Transportability of external strain surveillance margins
No waning of placebo under a common challenge distribution

novel.justification: This is a transparent restriction on the entire observable compatible-law fiber, not positivity of an observed trial cell. It is checkable by one linear program and is plausible when every response type allowed by the trial and exposure margins retains a policy-weighted period-two vaccine challenge risk bounded away from zero, as in challenge panels whose reference mixture assigns weight only to circulating variants with residual breakthrough susceptibility.

assumptions.condition: \(\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}\pi_a b_{tav}>0\) for every \(t\in\mathcal T\).

standard.name: Positive case incidence for a conditional strain distribution

definitions.name: Compatible full-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)=\{P\text{ on }(A,S,J^0,J^1,J):P\text{ satisfies }\text{ass:trial-randomization},\text{ ass:arm-positivity},\text{ ass:outcome-consistency},\text{ ass:no-vaccine-effect-on-exposure},\text{ ass:history-indexed-first-infection-map},\text{ ass:bounded-noninfecting-exposure-priming},\text{ ass:external-margin-transport},\text{ ass:placebo-reference-stability},\ P(J_t=v\mid A=a)=b_{tav}\text{ for every }(t,a,v)\in\mathcal T\times\mathcal A\times\mathcal V\}\).

definitions.name: Reduced common-history sensitivity polytope
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal S|}:\sum_sx_s=1;\ \sum_s\widetilde g_{tav}(s)x_s=b_{tav}\text{ for every }(t,a,v)\in\mathcal T\times\mathcal A\times\mathcal V;\ \sum_s\mathbf 1\{h_t^0=v\}x_s=q_{tv}\text{ for every }(t,v)\in\mathcal T\times\mathcal V_0;\ x_s=0\text{ if }h^0\neq h^1;\ \sum_{s,v}\omega_v\{r_{10v}(s)-r^{[0]}_{20v}(s)\}x_s=0;\ \sum_s\mathbf 1\{h_1^0=u,r_{1au}=0\}\mathbf 1\{r^{[u]}_{2av}\neq r^{[0]}_{2av}\}x_s\leq\delta\sum_s\mathbf 1\{h_1^0=u,r_{1au}=0\}x_s\text{ for every }(a,u,v)\in\mathcal A\times\mathcal V\times\mathcal V\}\).

definitions.name: Extended reciprocal image
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_{I,\delta}(b,q,\omega)=\{\rho_{11}(x,\omega)/\rho_{21}(x,\omega):x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega),\ \rho_{21}(x,\omega)>0\}\cup\{+\infty:\exists x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega),\ \rho_{21}(x,\omega)=0<\rho_{11}(x,\omega)\}\cup\bigl([0,+\infty]\text{ if }\exists x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega),\ \rho_{11}(x,\omega)=\rho_{21}(x,\omega)=0\bigr)\).

definitions.name: Reciprocal endpoint normalization
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_\delta(b,q,\omega)=\{(y,z)\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal S|}\times\mathbb R_+:\sum_sy_s=z;\ \sum_s\widetilde g_{tav}(s)y_s=b_{tav}z;\ \sum_s\mathbf 1\{h_t^0=v\}y_s=q_{tv}z;\ y_s=0\text{ if }h^0\neq h^1;\ \sum_{s,v}\omega_v\{r_{10v}(s)-r^{[0]}_{20v}(s)\}y_s=0;\ F_\delta y\leq0;\ \sum_{s,v}\omega_vr^{[0]}_{21v}(s)y_s=1\}\), where the two indexed equality families range over \(\mathcal T\times\mathcal A\times\mathcal V\) and \(\mathcal T\times\mathcal V_0\), respectively.

definitions.name: Canonical common-history linear system
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)=\{x\in\mathbb R_+^{|\overline{\mathcal S}|}:E_\omega x=d(b,q),\ F_\delta x\leq0\}\), with the omitted coordinates exactly the unequal-history types.

definitions.name: Point-mass challenge-estimand collapse handle
definitions.construction: For \(K=2\), place the four point-mass controlled challenge risks entering \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm P}_t(x)\), including the period-two no-prior-exposure responses \(R^{[0]}_{2av}\), on the positive comparison face of the fixed sensitivity fiber \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\). Use paired linear-fractional primal programs and Farkas certificates for the exposure-ratio and scaled-new-infection restrictions to determine whether the face is empty, whether \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm P}_t\) is nonconstant on a nonempty face, and whether a constant value on a nonempty face equals \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm{obs}}_t(b)\). Certify these three branches, respectively, by a separating infeasibility ray, two endpoint laws obtained through the common-history lift, or one compatible-law observable-mismatch witness whose controlled-risk value differs from the observed-hazard functional.

definitions.name: Worked two-variant compatible-law lift
definitions.construction: Set \(K=2\), \(\omega=\omega_\star^{(2)}\), \(b=b^{(2)}\), \(q=q^{(2)}\), and \(x=x_\star^{(2)}\). Draw \(S\) from \(x_\star^{(2)}\), draw \(A\) independently with probabilities \(\pi\), set \(H^0=H^1\) to the history carried by \(S\), define \(J_t^a\) by \(\mathbf 1\{J_t^a=v\}=\widetilde g_{tav}(S)\) with \(J_t^a=0\) when every such indicator is zero, and reveal \(J=J^A\). Because \(R^{[u]}_{2av}=R^{[0]}_{2av}\) for every \(u\), the lift satisfies the sensitivity restriction for every \(\delta\in[0,1]\).

definitions.name: External-margin redundancy handle
definitions.construction: Pointwise in \(\delta\), compare \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) with the substituted fiber \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q^{\mathrm{case}},\omega)\) by paired primal endpoint programs and their linear-program duals. Upon failure of endpoint invariance, the certificate reports exactly one exhaustive branch: a Farkas ray if the substituted fiber is empty; if it is nonempty and the ratio is nonconstant, two substituted-fiber compatible-law lifts with distinct ratio values plus an attaining primal endpoint law and matching dual bound that prove a strict mismatch with an original endpoint; or, if it is nonempty but ratio-constant, a primal compatible-law witness and matching dual endpoint bound proving that its singleton ratio set differs from the original sharp set. The last branch includes a singleton substituted fiber.

definitions.name: Common-law sign-radius handle
definitions.construction: At a fixed disclosed \(\delta\), keep the observed-data compatible fiber fixed at \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\). For each radius \(r\), optimize the sign contrast defining \(\Psi_{\omega'}(x)\) jointly over \(x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) and \(\omega'\in\Delta(\mathcal V)\) subject to \(\lVert\omega'-\omega\rVert_1\leq r\). Derive a primal attaining pair at the boundary and a dual robust-optimization cut certifying preservation of the baseline strict sign for every smaller radius; if the boundary set is empty, derive an infeasibility ray certifying \(r_\star(\delta)=+\infty\). The perturbation changes only the policy/reference functional: the trial risks \(b\), exposure margins \(q\), sensitivity value \(\delta\), common-history law \(x\), and placebo-stability row indexed by \(\omega\) are not rebuilt at \(\omega'\).

definitions.name: Exact simultaneous multinomial projection
definitions.construction: For a multinomial count vector \(u\) of total \(N\), let \(T_p(u)=2\{\ell_{\widehat p(u)}(u)-\ell_p(u)\}\), with \(0\log 0=0\), and define \(\operatorname{pv}_N(p;u)=\sum_{z:\sum_jz_j=N,\ T_p(z)\geq T_p(u)}\operatorname{Mult}_N(z;p)\) and \(\Gamma_N(u;\gamma)=\{p\in\Delta:\operatorname{pv}_N(p;u)\geq\gamma\}\). For each arm, use the multinomial categories \(\{\varnothing\}\cup(\mathcal T\times\mathcal V)\), with probabilities \(p^a_{tv}=b_{tav}\) and \(p^a_{\varnothing}=1-\sum_{t,v}b_{tav}\); for each period of the external sample, use categories \(\mathcal V_0\) with probabilities \(q_t\). Let \(\mathcal G_{n,m}(\alpha)\) contain every \(b',q'\) accepted by all four exact tests at level \(\alpha/4\), conditional on realized arm sizes. At fixed \(\delta\), define \(\mathcal C_{n,m,\delta}^{\mathrm{exact}}=\operatorname{cl}\bigcup_{(b',q')\in\mathcal G_{n,m}(\alpha):\mathcal P_\delta(b',q',\omega)\neq\varnothing}\Theta_{I,\delta}(b',q',\omega)\). This enumeration includes zero observed and zero candidate cells and uses no studentization or selected optimizer.

statements.statement: For every prespecified \(\delta\in[0,1]\), the projection of \(\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) onto the latent type-mass vector is exactly \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\). Every compatible full law induces one \(x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\), and every \(x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) lifts to a law in \(\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) reproducing \(b\), \(q\), \(\pi\), the history-indexed controlled responses, and the priming-fraction restriction.
statements.justification: Projection equality prevents a reduced optimizer under a disclosed priming sensitivity value from being mistaken for an unattainable collection of armwise or periodwise marginals.
statements.gap: Balke and Pearl (1997) establish the response-type template, while Janvin and Stensrud (2025) construct single-pathogen endpoint laws; neither gives this two-period variant-history projection with external margins and bounded noninfecting-exposure priming.
statements.consumer: Investigators combining vaccine trials with variant-surveillance panels obtain a finite feasibility test and full-law certificate for every reported bound.

statements.statement: For every prespecified \(\delta\in[0,1]\), if \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\neq\varnothing\), the extended set in \(\text{def:extended-ratio-image}\) is exactly the set of vaccine challenge-risk ratios compatible with \(\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)\). The finite positive-denominator values, the \(+\infty\) branch when \(\rho_{21}=0<\rho_{11}\), and the full \([0,+\infty]\) branch when \(\rho_{11}=\rho_{21}=0\) each have a compatible full-law certificate.
statements.justification: The causal identified set remains mathematically defined when no uniform lower bound on the vaccine reference risk is imposed.
statements.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) analyze finite single-pathogen ratios; the extended zero-denominator fibers created by changing variants and external margins are not covered by their endpoint formula.
statements.consumer: Analysts can report a valid sharp set, including infinite or completely unidentified branches, rather than silently deleting compatible zero-risk laws.

statements.statement: Fix \(\delta\in[0,1]\). If \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)=\varnothing\), the audit returns fiber infeasibility and does not certify \(\text{ass:reference-risk-positivity}\). If \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\neq\varnothing\), that restriction holds if and only if the linear program \(\min\{d_{21,\omega}^{\top}x:E_\omega x=d(b,q),\ F_\delta x\leq0,\ x\geq0\}\) has value at least \(\epsilon\). Equivalently, there are \(\eta\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) satisfying \(E_\omega^{\top}\eta-F_\delta^{\top}\kappa\leq d_{21,\omega}\) and \(d(b,q)^{\top}\eta\geq\epsilon\).
statements.justification: This implementation audit separates incompatible observed margins from a genuinely nonempty fiber whose late vaccine reference risk is uniformly positive.
statements.gap: This is an LP audit device for the optional denominator restriction, not a root identification contribution.
statements.consumer: Software can stop on an infeasible fiber and issue a primal value and dual certificate only after compatibility has been established.

statements.statement: Fix \(\delta\in[0,1]\). Under \(\text{ass:reference-risk-positivity}\), if \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\neq\varnothing\), then \(\Theta_{I,\delta}(b,q,\omega)=[L_\delta(b,q,\omega),U_\delta(b,q,\omega)]\subset[0,1/\epsilon]\). Its endpoints are attained by minimizing and maximizing \(\sum_{s,v}\omega_vr_{11v}(s)y_s\) over \(\mathcal C_\delta(b,q,\omega)\). Every optimizer has \(z>0\), maps to \(x=y/z\), and lifts through Theorem \(\text{thm:exact-history-compression}\) to an endpoint-attaining full law.
statements.justification: The theorem turns a nonlinear waning ratio into two finite linear programs without sacrificing sharpness or common-law attainability.
statements.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) give closed-form single-pathogen finite bounds, while Follmann and Huang (2018) use a parametric marked process; neither gives sharp policy-mixture reciprocal endpoints on an LP-certified positive common-history fiber.
statements.consumer: A trial analyst can report exact best- and worst-case reference-mixture waning using standard linear-program solvers and attach an auditable latent-law witness.

statements.statement: Fix \(\delta\in[0,1]\). Under \(\text{ass:reference-risk-positivity}\), every compatible value of \(\Psi_\omega\) is below one if and only if \(U_\delta(b,q,\omega)<1\), and every compatible value is above one if and only if \(L_\delta(b,q,\omega)>1\). Unity is compatible if and only if \(L_\delta(b,q,\omega)\leq1\leq U_\delta(b,q,\omega)\), and both strict sides are compatible if and only if \(L_\delta(b,q,\omega)<1<U_\delta(b,q,\omega)\). All assertions optimize one common \(x\) across periods.
statements.justification: This is endpoint algebra that calibrates the substantive common-law separation theorem to the named ratio.
statements.gap: The trichotomy is an implementation corollary of finite sharp endpoints and is not claimed as a root contribution.
statements.consumer: A reporting routine can translate computed endpoints into below-unity, above-unity, unity-compatible, or two-sided labels.

statements.statement: Fix \(\delta\in[0,1]\) and suppose \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\neq\varnothing\). Then \(\max_{x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)}c_\omega^{\top}x<0\) if and only if there are finite vectors \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\geq0\) such that \(E_\omega^{\top}\lambda+F_\delta^{\top}\mu\geq c_\omega\) componentwise and \(d(b,q)^{\top}\lambda<0\). Such a pair explicitly certifies \(\rho_{11}(x,\omega)<\rho_{21}(x,\omega)\) for every common-history law and hence a below-unity value of \(\Psi_\omega(x)\). Symmetrically, every compatible value is above one if and only if there are finite \(\eta\) and \(\kappa\geq0\) such that \(E_\omega^{\top}\eta-F_\delta^{\top}\kappa\leq c_\omega\) and \(d(b,q)^{\top}\eta>0\). When either certificate fails, the corresponding primal optimizer lifts to a compatible full law on the noncertified side.
statements.justification: The certificate prices every period, arm, variant, exposure-margin, placebo-stability, and priming-sensitivity row with one coherent set of multipliers and supplies a compatible counterlaw when separation fails.
statements.gap: Tomer and Biccler (2022) exhibit mixture-driven temporal movement under specified mechanisms, but do not derive an observable separation theorem over one external-margin common-history sensitivity fiber.
statements.consumer: Regulators can audit a robust below-unity conclusion from reported multipliers and recover an attainable counterexample law whenever the certificate fails.

statements.statement: For any \(x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) satisfying \(\rho_{10}(x,\omega)=\rho_{20}(x,\omega)>0\), and under \(\text{ass:reference-risk-positivity}\), the singleton value of \(\Psi_\omega(x)\) is below one if and only if \(\operatorname{VE}_1(x)>\operatorname{VE}_2(x)\), so biological vaccine effect wanes; it is above one if and only if \(\operatorname{VE}_1(x)<\operatorname{VE}_2(x)\), so biological vaccine effect strengthens.
statements.justification: This calibration records the extra positive-placebo condition needed to interpret ratio direction biologically.
statements.gap: The identity is positive-denominator algebra and is not claimed as a root contribution.
statements.consumer: Booster-timing committees can separate a formally certified ratio statement from the extra condition required for a biological vaccine-effect interpretation.

statements.statement: For every \(\delta\in[0,1]\), the construction in \(\text{def:k2-worked-lift}\) satisfies \(x_\star^{(2)}\in\mathcal P_\delta(b^{(2)},q^{(2)},\omega_\star^{(2)})\) and its displayed full law belongs to \(\mathfrak M_\delta(b^{(2)},q^{(2)},\omega_\star^{(2)})\). It yields the displayed nonzero trial risks, uniform exposure margins, \(\rho_{t0}(x_\star^{(2)},\omega_\star^{(2)})=\rho_{t1}(x_\star^{(2)},\omega_\star^{(2)})=1/2\) for \(t=1,2\), and \(\Psi_{\omega_\star^{(2)}}(x_\star^{(2)})=\{1\}\).
statements.justification: The numerical lift exposes every step from one common exposure history through observed strain risks to a compatible full law.
statements.gap: This is a worked certificate for the new multi-variant compression, not a standalone novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Readers and software implementers obtain a four-atom regression test for feasibility, lifting, and ratio evaluation.

statements.statement: When \(K=1\), \(\delta=0\), \(q_{11}=q_{21}=1\), and \(\omega_1=1\), the period-two no-prior-exposure controlled challenge risk in each arm obeys \(b_{2a1}\leq\rho_{2a}(x,\omega)\leq b_{1a1}+b_{2a1}\), the risk inclusion used in the proof of Theorem 1 of Janvin and Stensrud (2025).
statements.justification: The no-priming endpoint \(\delta=0\) checks that the expanded history construction preserves the standard one-pathogen survivor-selection geometry.
statements.gap: This is a required calibration to Janvin and Stensrud (2025), not a claimed novelty.
statements.consumer: Readers can verify the new program against the established one-pathogen proof boundary before using variant margins.

statements.statement: If only \(\delta\in\mathcal D\) is scientifically justified, then \(\Theta_I^{\mathcal D}(b,q,\omega)\) is the sharp closed identified set over \(\bigcup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)\). A uniform below-unity conclusion holds exactly when \(\sup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\max_{x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)}c_\omega^{\top}x<0\); a uniform above-unity conclusion is obtained by the symmetric minimum criterion. Reports give the pointwise sets and sign certificates over \(\delta\in\mathcal D\) together with this envelope; absent controlled validation, \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\).
statements.justification: The sensitivity parameter is scientifically interpretable only through a prespecified range, so identification and sign reporting must aggregate the same pointwise compatible-law analyses.
statements.gap: Existing vaccine challenge-effect bounds do not provide a sharp envelope over a bounded noninfecting-exposure priming fraction.
statements.consumer: Trial analysts can display exactly which ratio and sign conclusions survive the scientifically defensible priming range, including the unrestricted range when no validation substudy exists.

statements.statement: Pointwise in each reported \(\delta\in\mathcal D\), derive necessary and sufficient observable dual conditions under which replacing the external exposure margin \(q\) by \(q^{\mathrm{case}}\) leaves both sharp endpoints \(L_\delta\) and \(U_\delta\) unchanged. When these conditions fail, the certificate must cover the exhaustive partition: if \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q^{\mathrm{case}},\omega)=\varnothing\), give a finite Farkas certificate of incompatible substituted margins; if that fiber is nonempty and \(\Psi_\omega\) is nonconstant on it, give two compatible full-law lifts with the same \(b\) and \(q^{\mathrm{case}}\) but different ratio values, together with an attaining primal endpoint law and matching dual bound proving a strict mismatch with \(L_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) or \(U_\delta(b,q,\omega)\); if that fiber is nonempty but ratio-constant, including when it is a singleton, give a compatible-law primal witness and matching dual endpoint bound proving that its singleton sharp ratio set differs strictly from \(\Theta_{I,\delta}(b,q,\omega)\).
statements.justification: Case strains are selected by infection and can coincide with exposure margins only on a mathematically characterizable invariance frontier.
statements.gap: Gilbert et al. (2001) and van der Laan and Gilbert (2023) give sufficient case-only interpretations under exposure restrictions, but not an if-and-only-if sharp-set preservation criterion.
statements.consumer: Surveillance analysts learn exactly when readily available breakthrough-strain frequencies can replace costly exposure surveillance and when they cannot.

statements.statement: For \(K=2\), each \(t\in\mathcal T\), and each reported \(\delta\in\mathcal D\), characterize necessary and sufficient restrictions under which, on the face where all component risks and at-risk denominators are positive, \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm P}_t(x)\) is constant over \(x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) and equals \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm{obs}}_t(b)\). When the restrictions fail, the certificate must cover the exhaustive partition: give a finite separating certificate if the comparison face is empty; if it is nonempty and \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm P}_t\) is nonconstant, construct two vectors on that face whose compatible full-law lifts yield different values; if it is nonempty and \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm P}_t\) is constant but that constant differs from \(\operatorname{CSE}^{\mathrm{obs}}_t(b)\), give one compatible-law lift on the face and its controlled-risk calculation as an observable-mismatch certificate.
statements.justification: The adjacent point-identification result should enter the larger external-margin analysis through an exact collapse boundary, not through an asserted class inclusion.
statements.gap: Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5 and Proposition on marginal \(CSE_k\) identification) identify the time-to-event challenge subtype effect from at-risk event hazards under time-to-event exchangeability, positivity, consistency, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, a covariate-invariant exposure ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality; they do not characterize the identified set after those last identification restrictions are replaced by external exposure margins and a common-history fiber.
statements.consumer: Vaccine researchers can determine when the published point-identified challenge subtype effect is recovered and when external surveillance supports only a nondegenerate compatible-law set.

statements.statement: At each reported \(\delta\in\mathcal D\), whenever the pooled frontier at \(\omega\) certifies one strict common sign, determine \(r_\star(\delta)\) from its finite-dimensional common-law optimization. The candidate \(\omega'\) changes only \(\Psi_{\omega'}(x)\): every candidate law remains in the fixed fiber \(x\in\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\), whose trial-risk, external-margin, priming-sensitivity, common-history, and placebo-stability constraints remain indexed by \(b\), \(q\), \(\delta\), and \(\omega\). If \(r_\star(\delta)<+\infty\), produce an attaining compatible-law pair \((x,\omega')\) at which the strict side first fails. For every \(r<r_\star(\delta)\), produce a dual certificate that all feasible \(x\) and all \(\omega'\) with \(\lVert\omega'-\omega\rVert_1\leq r\) retain that side. If reversal is infeasible for every \(\omega'\), establish \(r_\star(\delta)=+\infty\) with a dual infeasibility certificate.
statements.justification: A sign verdict is decision-relevant only together with the smallest reference-policy change that defeats it while holding the trial, exposure margins, and compatible-law restrictions fixed.
statements.gap: Tomer and Biccler (2022) establish mixture-driven time variation, but no published result located gives a fixed-fiber common-law policy radius with an attaining witness, certificates below the radius, and an infinity branch.
statements.consumer: Policy makers choosing a reference strain portfolio obtain an auditable robustness radius that does not silently reinterpret the observed trial under each counterfactual mixture.

statements.statement: For \(\mathcal C_{n,m,\delta}^{\mathrm{exact}}\) at a prespecified \(\delta\), establish \(\Pr\{\Theta_{I,\delta}(b,q,\omega)\subseteq\mathcal C_{n,m,\delta}^{\mathrm{exact}}\}\geq1-\alpha\), conditional on realized treatment-arm sample sizes, for every law in \(\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)\) and every external sampling law in the stated sampling model, including zero trial or exposure cells and extended zero-denominator branches. Derive a finite computational representation of the projected closed set that preserves empty candidate fibers and does not select an endpoint optimizer.
statements.justification: Exact primitive-cell inversion makes whole-set coverage definite at zero counts and leaves only the nontrivial projection geometry to resolve.
statements.gap: Romano and Shaikh (2010) give general whole-set coverage and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) give calibrated projection, but neither derives this finite exact multinomial projection through extended reciprocal common-history fibers.
statements.consumer: Regulators obtain a finite-sample confidence statement for every compatible ratio value without asymptotic rate restrictions or ad hoc zero-cell corrections.

sampling_model.design: A two-arm randomized vaccine trial is combined with an external exposure-surveillance sample from the same period-specific target environment.
sampling_model.units: Trial participants are independent draws. Conditional on each realized arm size, the mutually exclusive categories consisting of no first infection and first infection by period and variant are multinomial. Each period-specific external exposure count is multinomial on \(\mathcal V_0\); arbitrary dependence between the two period margins for the same surveillance units is allowed because simultaneous coverage uses a union bound.
sampling_model.treatment: \(A\in\{0,1\}\) has known probabilities \(\pi\), and the trial records the period and variant of each first infection.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-arm positivity is standard. Noninfecting-exposure priming is indexed by the disclosed sensitivity value \(\delta\), with \(\delta=0\) giving no priming and \(\delta=1\) permitting unrestricted priming. Fiber-wide period-two vaccine reference-risk positivity is a separate novel, LP-checkable restriction used only for finite Charnes--Cooper endpoints; the extended identified set and exact projection allow zero denominators.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The trial and exposure cell probabilities are covered by exact likelihood-ratio-ordered multinomial inversions at Bonferroni level \(\alpha/4\) for each of two arms and two periods. Zero observed and zero candidate cells are permitted. The sensitivity range \(\mathcal D\) is fixed outside these samples; routine negative tests or serial serology do not identify a small \(\delta\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 derives sharp two-period bounds for a single-pathogen challenge effect from conventional vaccine-trial risks.
Section 4 shows that multi-variant vaccine-effectiveness measures can be time-varying under leaky and all-or-none mechanisms.
The weighted estimating-equation model permits time-varying vaccine efficacy and time-varying pathogen distributions under a marked exposure process.
Case-only strain odds ratios receive a biological relative-efficacy interpretation under stated exposure and susceptibility conditions.
Theorems 1 through 3 identify conditional relative strain efficacy from case-only data under explicit missingness and causal assumptions.
Finite latent response types and linear programming yield tight treatment-effect bounds and attaining distributions.
The paper constructs random regions with uniform asymptotic coverage of an entire identified set or its known image.
Calibrated bootstrap projection gives uniformly valid intervals for smooth functions of moment-constrained partially identified parameters.
Derivative-aware resampling is valid for directionally differentiable maps in settings where the ordinary bootstrap can fail.
The paper develops a powerful single-pathogen test of treatment-effect constancy and additional waning bounds.

Section 5 defines the marginal time-to-event challenge subtype effect, and the marginal-identification proposition identifies it as a ratio of two observed cause-specific hazard ratios under the paper's stated time-to-event identification and proportionality assumptions.

tldr: Changing pathogen variants make early-versus-late vaccine challenge risk depend on one latent coupling of exposures and responses across periods. The response type now permits a noninfecting period-one exposure to alter later controlled susceptibility, and a disclosed \(\delta\in[0,1]\) bounds the altered fraction; \(\delta=0\) gives no priming and \(\delta=1\) is unrestricted. Pointwise in \(\delta\), one finite common-history polytope exactly represents every law compatible with randomized-trial risks and external exposure margins, its extended reference-mixture ratio set remains sharp at zero denominators, finite reciprocal endpoints follow under the separate LP-audited denominator condition, and a common-law dual certifies strict ratio signs. Results are reported pointwise and over a scientifically justified range \(\mathcal D\), defaulting to \([0,1]\) without a randomized or controlled validation substudy. Open questions cover the Perényi--Stensrud collapse boundary, case-frequency substitution, fixed-fiber policy-mixture sign robustness, and exact multinomial whole-set projection.

project_justification.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) give sharp single-pathogen challenge-effect bounds, and Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5) identify a variant-specific time-to-event challenge subtype effect under exposure and proportionality restrictions. Neither gives a sharp common-history ratio set from trial first-infection risks plus external variant-exposure margins when a prior exposure that did not infect may alter later controlled susceptibility, nor an observable sign certificate valid pointwise over a disclosed bound on that priming.
project_justification.niche: The target compares one policy-fixed reference mixture across periods and defines period-two challenge risk after no period-one exposure. A history-indexed response array separates that target response from the response after a noninfecting exposure; the linear sensitivity value \(\delta\) then restricts their disagreement without replacing external exposure margins by selected case-strain frequencies. Routine negative tests and serial serology do not justify a small \(\delta\), so analysis without a controlled validation substudy spans \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\).
project_justification.fill: The substantive chain supplies, pointwise in \(\delta\), exact common-history compression, an always-defined extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the disclosed denominator condition, and a common-law sign dual with compatible counterlaws. A sensitivity-range envelope reports the set and sign conclusion over \(\mathcal D\). Positivity duality, endpoint sign algebra, biological translation, and the \(K=2\) no-priming lift remain audit or calibration results; the collapse, substitution, radius, and exact-inference frontiers remain open.

related_work: Janvin and Stensrud (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix B) establish sharp finite single-pathogen two-period challenge-effect bounds and attaining laws; their multiple-version analysis does not retain external period-specific variant margins or index later controlled response by a prior noninfecting exposure. Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5 and the marginal \(CSE_k\) identification proposition) define a time-to-event challenge subtype effect from point-mass controlled-exposure risks and identify it by observed cause-specific hazards under time-to-event exchangeability, positivity, consistency, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, a covariate-invariant exposure ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality. Their causal coordinates are represented here using \(\rho_{ta}(x,e^{(v)})\), with the period-two coordinate explicitly based on \(R^{[0]}_{2av}\); the present external-margin sensitivity fiber is informed by that estimand but does not claim a theorem-level class-inclusion boundary, which remains \(\text{oeq:perenyi-collapse-boundary}\). Tomer and Biccler (2022) show that competing variants can generate temporal movement under specified mechanisms, but do not give a common-history sign certificate under bounded noninfecting-exposure priming or a fixed-fiber mixture radius. Follmann and Huang (2018) use a marked exposure-process model. Gilbert et al. (2001), Edlefsen (2014), and van der Laan and Gilbert (2023) explain why selected infecting strains require extra exposure and susceptibility restrictions, so case frequencies are not substituted for the external exposure margins \(q\). Balke and Pearl (1997) inform the finite response-type lift. Romano and Shaikh (2010) and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) inform whole-set projection; the open inference question instead fixes exact multinomial inversion allowing zero cells and projects each \(\delta\)-fiber and its prespecified sensitivity envelope.
technical_internal_limitation: The parameter \(\delta\) controls whether a single period-one exposure that did not infect changes the period-two controlled response relative to no prior exposure. Routine negative tests establish noninfection, not absence of immune priming, and serial serology need not detect response-relevant cellular or mucosal changes; neither identifies a small \(\delta\). Without a randomized or controlled validation substudy, the honest sensitivity range is \(\mathcal D=[0,1]\). The finite map still abstracts from multiple distinct noninfecting exposures within one period.
honest_scope: Exact common-history projection, the unconditional extended sharp set, finite attained reciprocal endpoints under the separately disclosed fiber-wide denominator condition, and common-history sign separation are substantive claims pointwise in prespecified \(\delta\). The target period-two risk uses \(R^{[0]}_{21v}\), while observed period-two infections use \(R^{[H_1]}_{2av}\); their discrepancy among noninfected exposees is bounded, not suppressed. The report gives pointwise results and the sharp envelope over a scientifically justified \(\mathcal D\), using \([0,1]\) without controlled validation. Fiber infeasibility is failure and never vacuous positivity. Positivity duality, endpoint sign trichotomy, positive-placebo biological translation, the \(K=2\) lift, and the \(K=1,\delta=0\) reduction are implementation or calibration results. The Perényi--Stensrud collapse boundary, case-frequency invariance, fixed-fiber mixture radius, and exact multinomial projection remain open. External exposure margins remain primitives; pooled case-strain frequencies do not replace them.

novelty_justification: The kernel is the exact projection of one probability vector that simultaneously indexes both latent period-by-variant exposure histories and history-indexed controlled responses. A linear sensitivity restriction bounds the proportion of noninfected period-one exposees for whom \(R^{[u]}_{2av}\) differs from the no-prior-exposure target response \(R^{[0]}_{2av}\), yielding a nested continuum from no priming at \(\delta=0\) to unrestricted priming at \(\delta=1\). Pointwise in \(\delta\), the projection yields an extended reciprocal image at zero denominators, finite attained endpoints under a separate LP-checkable denominator restriction, and a substantive dual separation theorem that includes the sensitivity inequalities. Perényi and Stensrud (2025, Section 5) inform the point-mass challenge-risk coordinates, but their observed-hazard identification uses stronger exposure-ratio and scaled-new-infection restrictions; equality with their functional is kept as an open boundary rather than a theorem-level comparator promise. The sensitivity-range envelope makes explicit that routine negative tests or serial serology do not identify a small \(\delta\).
